correlates.name: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein purpura)
correlates.presentation: A 4-year-old boy has crampy abdominal pain 2 weeks after a cold and will not use his right hand, whose wrist is swollen. A raised, lumpy, red-purple rash that does not fade under pressure covers his buttocks, the backs of his legs and his elbows. T 38.2 C, BP 102/64.
correlates.workup: Platelets 310,000 and coagulation normal; urinalysis shows white cells and microscopic hematuria, yet the urine culture is negative; BUN and creatinine normal.
correlates.management: Supportive care; steroids may ease the abdominal pain. Most children recover fully, but follow the kidney (urinalysis, BP) long term. Worsening abdominal pain: exclude intussusception with an enema.

correlates.name: Testicular torsion
correlates.presentation: An 8-year-old boy came home from school 2 hours ago walking hunched over, holding his lower abdomen; he vomited once. The abdomen is soft and nontender, but the left testicle is swollen, very tender and sits higher than the right. Stroking the left inner thigh does not lift it.
correlates.workup: Doppler ultrasound of the scrotum: no blood flow to the swollen left testicle; normal flow on the right.
correlates.management: Straight to the ER and urology - the testicle dies within hours of pain onset. Untwist it surgically and tack down BOTH testicles, since the free-hanging attachment is usually bilateral; do not wait for an afternoon clinic slot.

correlates.name: Torsion of the appendix testis
correlates.presentation: A 10-year-old boy has a day of right scrotal pain that built up gradually. The pain is confined to a pea-sized tender nodule at the upper pole of the right testicle, visible through the skin as a small dark-blue spot. The rest is nontender and normally placed; reflex intact.
correlates.management: Symptomatic: NSAIDs and ice, and reassure - it is benign. If the picture is not this clearly localized, send for Doppler ultrasound to rule out a twisted testicle.

correlates.name: Imperforate hymen
correlates.presentation: A 13-year-old girl had a growth spurt and Tanner 4 breast development but has never had a period. For 5 months she has had monthly lower abdominal, low back and bladder-area pain lasting several days. She voids normally. A tense, bluish bulge fills the vaginal opening.
correlates.workup: Pelvic ultrasound: the vagina is distended with layered fluid (trapped menstrual blood) that presses on the bladder; both renal pelves mildly dilated.

correlates.name: Ovarian torsion
correlates.presentation: A 15-year-old girl has 3 hours of sudden, severe right lower abdominal pain with repeated vomiting; her family thinks it is a stomach bug. Afebrile, HR 112, BP 118/74. Right lower quadrant tender without rebound; urine pregnancy test negative; periods regular.
correlates.workup: Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler: an enlarged right ovary with little or no blood flow; appendix not seen to be inflamed.
